title: Review of Measures and Help Provided in Student Bullying Incidents
what_it_is: Review of Measures and Help Provided in Student Bullying Incidents

sections.label: Parliamentary questions on school bullying
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Education about teacher training, prevention, police collaboration, reporting numbers, tracking and anti-bullying policies in schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether teachers are sufficiently equipped with the knowledge and skills to identify and manage bullying, especially in cases where victims do not report incidents; and (b) what measures are in place to ensure schools have adequate trained personnel, such as counsellors and disciplinary staff, to support teachers and students in handling bullying cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what steps are taken by the Ministry and schools to prevent occurrences of bullying incidents in schools; (b) what is the level of collaboration between schools and the Singapore Police Force in cases where the bullying of students happen outside of the schools; and (c) whether there are adequate monitoring and surveillance to pick up early indications of bullying situations and what are the pre-emptive and preventive measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) in each year of the past five years, how many reports has the Ministry received regarding incidents of bullying that occurred within or outside of school premises; and (b) in view of the recent bullying incidents at an Institute of Technical Education campus, a secondary school and a primary school, whether the Ministry currently has in place an anti-bullying policy at all schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry tracks the number of reported bullying cases in schools; (b) if so, what is the number of bullying cases in each year of the last five years; (c) if not, why not; and (d) what resources and policies are being put in place in schools to enhance the detection, reporting and correction of bullying cases.

sections.label: Bullying incident rates per students
sections.summary: Annually, primary schools averaged two and secondary schools six bullying incidents per 1,000 students, with technology-related incidents fewer than one per 1,000 secondary students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For every 1,000 students, there were an average of two incidents in primary schools and six incidents in secondary schools annually for any form of bullying, both within and outside of school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Of these, incidents involving the use of technology averaged less than one incident per 1,000 secondary students and even fewer in primary schools each year.

sections.label: Caning and police reports for bullying
sections.summary: Caning is a last resort for boys by authorised adults, and severe bullying or fights lead to Police reports and legal consequences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Caning is used as a last resort for boys and carried out in an appropriate manner only by authorised adults.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For severe bullying or fights, a Police report will be made and perpetrators will face legal consequences in accordance with the law.

sections.label: Doxxing and ostracising perpetrators
sections.summary: Circulating materials, doxxing or calling for ostracism of student perpetrators could isolate them more, drive them to extremes and hinder their reform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Circulating such materials, trying to doxx the student perpetrators or calling for them to be ostracised, could isolate them even more, drive them to extremes and make it harder for them to mend their ways.

sections.label: MOE reviewing bullying management strategies
sections.summary: MOE will work with schools to share good practices, review bullying management strategies, update education and intervention measures, and partner parents for safe learning environments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: MOE will continue to work with schools to share good practices and review the strategies to manage bullying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will continue to update these education and intervention measures and partner parents to create caring and safe learning environments for our students.

sections.label: Supporting rehabilitation of perpetrators
sections.summary: Everyone has the power and duty to support each other and foster healing and change, avoiding actions like counter-productive social media behaviours that hinder a perpetrator's rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We all hold the power and duty to support each other and to foster an environment where healing and change are possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We want to steer clear of actions that might hinder or deny a perpetrator's chance for rehabilitation, such as counter-productive social media behaviours.

sections.label: Counsellor ratio in schools
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry ensures schools keep an adequate counsellor-to-student ratio, especially schools with more bullying.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How does the Ministry ensure that schools maintain an adequate ratio of counsellors to support students, particularly those schools that may have a higher incidence of bullying?

sections.label: Counsellors reinforced by needs
sections.summary: All schools have a baseline number of counsellors, reinforced according to specific needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: One, while all schools have a baseline number of counsellors, they are reinforced according to the specific needs.

sections.label: Punishment considers circumstances and background
sections.summary: Any punishment or rehabilitation must consider the circumstances and background of both victim and perpetrator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Any punishment or rehabilitation must take into account the circumstances and also the background of both the victim and perpetrator.

sections.label: Varying interpretations of bullying
sections.summary: Interpretations of bullying vary, and some people manage incidents without escalating them to adults or teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: What people constitute as "bullying" also varies in interpretation across different people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: There will be instances whereby some people may have encountered some bullying or unfortunate instances and where they think that they are able to manage it and they did not escalate the issue to the adults or teachers.

sections.label: Reported online cases lower
sections.summary: The number of reported online cases is generally much lower than offline ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The number of reported online cases is generally much lower than the offline ones.

sections.label: Online reports may rise
sections.summary: The speaker believes online numbers will progressively rise due to children's circumstances and greater awareness leading to more reported instances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It has to be taken in context and then we have to look at the case carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, my own belief is that the online numbers will progressively rise because of the circumstances that our children are exposed to, but also because as people become more aware of what is happening, there will be more of such reported instances.

sections.label: Bullying guidelines and remediation measures
sections.summary: Bullying guidelines are the same, but remediation measures depend on victims' and perpetrators' conditions and circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The guidelines as to what constitutes bullying is the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But the remediation measures will have to be taken in context, taking into account the conditions and circumstances of both the victims and the perpetrators.

sections.label: Classification change for out-of-school instances
sections.summary: The classification change is that instances outside school, previously not accounted for, are now included in the data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The only thing that we have changed in the classification is that, previously, we did not account for instances that happened outside of school, but more recently, we have also put that into our data.

sections.label: Risks of viral videos
sections.summary: It can lead to people trying to out-viral the last known video, and care is needed when viralling such things.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Second, it can lead to people trying to "out-viral" the last known video.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But third, we have to have a care when we viral such things.

sections.label: Care over suggested actions and digital footprint
sections.summary: Suggested actions need care because they will leave a digital footprint for a very long time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Sometimes, the things that they suggest we do, we need to have a care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It will leave a digital footprint for a very long time.

sections.label: Parental partnership in rehabilitation
sections.summary: Rehabilitation cannot be done independent of parents, who are partners, and there is no position of fining or punishing parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The rehabilitation process cannot be done independent of the parents because the parents are part of the partnership for us to bring up the children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We do not have a position, as the Member has mentioned, like in some other jurisdictions, where they take the parents to task through fines or other punitive measures.

sections.label: Doxxing, social vigilantism and platforms
sections.summary: Doxxing occurs regardless of student age, social vigilantism can backfire and complicate helping victims and rehabilitating perpetrators, and platform companies will be explored with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It could be younger students; it could be older students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It does not matter; it is still doxxing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, sometimes, when people exercise what I call "social vigilantism", it can backfire and complicate many of the efforts to help the victim and to rehabilitate the perpetrators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will continue to explore with the platform companies to see what can be done.
